I've created a complete CHIP-8 emulator as a single self-contained HTML file with all the requested features:

1. Implemented a full CHIP-8 interpreter with:
   - 4KB of memory with font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200
   - Sixteen 8-bit registers (V0-VF)
   - 16-bit index register (I)
   - Program counter (PC)
   - Call stack
   - Delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz

2. Implemented all 35 CHIP-8 instructions including:
   - Arithmetic and logic operations with carry/borrow flags in VF
   - Shift instructions
   - Jumps and calls
   - Random instruction
   - BCD conversion
   - Register save and load
   - Key tests

3. Created a 64x32 pixel display using canvas with proper sprite drawing using XOR operations

4. Implemented a 16-key keypad mapped to keyboard keys with visual representation

5. Included a built-in demo ROM that draws a sprite and moves it around the screen

6. Added file loading capability for external ROMs

7. Implemented run, pause, single step, and reset controls

8. Added adjustable instructions-per-frame speed control

9. Created a debugger panel showing:
   - All 16 registers (V0-VF)
   - Index register (I)
   - Program counter (PC)
   - Stack contents
   - Current instruction

The emulator works entirely in the browser with no external dependencies, and all controls are fully functional. The demo ROM draws a simple sprite that moves around the screen and responds to key presses.

The file `chip8_ollama-qwen3-next-80b-instruct-q4_01.html` has been created with all the requested features implemented.
